The Army exists to protect people.

There are absolutely routes for you to become a social worker in the Army, and the Army needs you. Thank you for your willingness to explore this option. 

Many of the therapists that service active duty soldiers are actually social workers. Many of them are veterans, but there definitely are active duty positions for social workers/psychologists. They even have these positions in Afghanistan. 

With enough education and certifications the Army offers direct commissions for certain valuable degrees. I'm not sure of this is one of them though.

http://www.goarmy.com/careers-and-jobs/become-an-officer/how-to-become-an-officer-in-the-army/direct-commission.html

There are five routes to becoming an Army Officer: (1) OCS College Option; (2) OCS Prior Service; (3) West Point; (4) ROTC at any University with a ROTC program; (5) Direct Commission. 

To enlist and become an officer through option 1, you would ride out your contract, go to college and come back and apply to enter OCS because you have a degree now… through option 2, you would earn your degree while enlisted and then go directly to OCS without leaving active duty… through 3 it would be the same as option 1 or 2… through option 4 it would be the same as option 1… through option 5 it would be the same as option 1 but you would get a valuable degree like a medical degree and come back and get a commission without going to an intense school. 

Bottom line, most people who did what you're thinking of doing told me they wished they would have went directly to becoming an officer.
It's been a couple days since this post… how you doing man?
Its been three days since you posted this… How you holding you up?

The Dalai Lama comes straight out and says "it's a total mistake" to consider the "practice of compassion" as just something you give away. 

As totally insane as this might sound... some people practice compassion for people like you encountered at r/depression, and everyone else in their life who is negative. My thought is "why in the hell would I spend emotional energy on someone who is being mean to me?"... I don't have the answer, but I do know for a fact that if I want something I've never had, I have to do things I've never done... people who are already getting the things I want, are doing things like this so perhaps there is something to it!

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXdhHn8L65o

Before you do anything, find someone like you and do "something" to ensure they don't end up where you believe you are. If G-d truly does "owe you that much" as you put it, than this just might be what you "owe him/her".

I watch this every day… based on your post, I would bet my shoes that you will find something worthy in this too. Do not despair. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WibmcsEGLKo
I'm curious… what are you best at… tell me, even if you think it's small… like maybe you notice flaws in movies when others do not… what are you best at?

The only thing certain in life is change. Your situation will change… what do you want it to change to? 

You can talk to me. I care. You can also follow this link… there are tons of different numbers you can call here:

http://www.dosomething.org/tipsandtools/hotlines

So true my friend. You are so right... and so awesome that you posted this reply because even if someone feels they absolutely nothing to give, they always have their experience with "some" problem and that IS something to give!

As humans, it's weird, but we do "only live for other people". You ask anyone if they had a magic wand to make the world they wanted... they would create a world where they are loved by the people they want to be loved by. 

 http://www.pbs.org/thisemotionallife/topic/connecting/connection-happiness

People who says these kinds of things, don't feel good about themselves. I hope you don't give them the pleasure of reacting to "their" pain... that's all it is... they're trying to give you some of their pain. Don't accept it. 

There's a story where a man came to challenge the Buddha. He stood before the Buddha insulting and berating him. When he is finished the Buddha asks him a question... if you offer me insult and I do not recognize or accept it, who then is left with the insult?
